scope: Theorem A.7 (Quasipolynomial inverse theorem) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 91. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer s ≥ 1. Let p ≥ 2. A unit- bounded function on an interval whose Us+1 norm is at least e−p correlates by at least B(p)−1 with a unit-bounded degree-s niltest of complexity P(p). The same conclusion holds on integer boxes and on products of cyclic groups, with the following dimension convention: for every fixed A ≥ 1, dimension n ≤ (2 + p)A is permitted, and the constants and polynomial exponents may depend only on s, A. On a product of cyclic groups the niltest is evaluated in the coordinatewise integer representatives.
